key_insight: Adding differential privacy to federated learning creates a measurable trade-off: stronger privacy noise reduces accuracy and destabilizes feature-attribution explanations, but model simplification and careful DP tuning can recover interpretable behavior without sacrificing much utility.
problem_solved: Clarifies how differential privacy affects model explainability in federated learning and provides empirical guidance to balance privacy, accuracy and interpretability in distributed ML systems.
method: Systematic empirical study comparing FL models trained with and without DP across datasets, measuring accuracy, feature-attribution stability (e.g., SHAP/LIME-style metrics) and feature sparsity.
Analysis of model complexity (feature count, architecture depth) and DP noise levels to identify configurations that preserve explainability.
Derive practical recommendations for configuring DP parameters and model design to mitigate negative impacts on explanations.
impact: Enables ML engineers and researchers to make informed trade-offs when deploying privacy-preserving federated models, helping maintain trustworthy, interpretable predictions in privacy-sensitive applications.
visual_elements: 3‑axis trade-off plot (privacy ε vs. accuracy vs. explanation stability) showing Pareto frontier
Side‑by‑side feature‑attribution heatmaps before and after applying DP to illustrate explanation drift
Bar chart of feature importance stability or sparsity as DP noise increases
Pipeline diagram of a federated learning system with DP injection points and XAI evaluation module
paper_title: Towards Explainable Federated Learning: Understanding the Impact of Differential Privacy
paper_authors: Júlio Oliveira, Rodrigo Ferreira, André Riker, Glaucio H. S. Carvalho, Eirini Eleni Tsilopoulou
